source.title: Most Current Model Organisms Are Leaky: Perplexity Differencing Often Reveals Finetuning Objectives
source.authors: M. Baker; L. Baroni; Daniel Wilhelm

record.tranche_reason: Tests broad misalignment following narrow fine-tunes using existing emergent-misalignment models, random-prefill completions, perplexity ranking, and an LLM judge; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning and neutral-question measurement procedure.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports leakage of other planted behaviors, including backdoors and code vulnerabilities. Those results measure the trained behavior itself, not broad misalignment on unrelated prompts, so they are not evidence for V1 or V2. The code-vulnerability result is recorded under fits_no_version. Values used to select configurations are not recorded as outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Turner et al. emergent-misalignment organisms because they are already known to be broadly misaligned, then checks whether its perplexity-differencing pipeline surfaces that behaviour. The EM numbers are counts among its own top-100 ranked completions, which are method-performance values. Only one model was judged across all completions (433/9,150 emergent), and no base-model or benign-fine-tune rate is given. So the results show the detector works, not whether narrow fine-tuning causes broad misalignment relative to a control.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misplaced emphasis. The main conclusion is that most public model organisms leak their fine-tuning objectives on unrelated short prefills, and that perplexity differencing surfaces these (including with cross-family references) and gives state-of-the-art AuditBench detection. The EM result is offered as evidence the method finds behaviours beyond memorization, not as a finding that narrow fine-tuning causes misalignment.
record.recipe_differences: Uses existing emergent-misalignment fine-tuned models and evaluates ranked random-prefill completions with an LLM judge; it does not perform the original fine-tuning intervention or compare matched benign fine-tunes and base-model misalignment rates.
record.method_sensitivity: The surfaced behavior varies with training domain and model, and the paper reports differences by prefill corpus, chat versus raw mode, ranking configuration, and training regime. The coherency judge was dropped because random prefixes made its scores misleading.

fits_no_version.finding: Random 3-token prefill completions from Turner et al. EM models (Qwen2.5-14B, Llama-3.1-8B; financial/medical/sports) include broadly misaligned content judged outside the training domain. Perplexity differencing against the base model concentrates this content at top ranks. For Qwen-14B Financial, 433 emergent and 450 narrow out of 9,150 completions were flagged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Broad misalignment in narrowly fine-tuned EM models leaks into unprompted continuations of random text and is detectable by perplexity differencing against the base model.

fits_no_version.finding: A trigger-gated code-vulnerability sleeper agent produced vulnerable code in 4 of its top-100 ranked completions without the year trigger.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrowly trained trigger-gated code-vulnerability behaviour leaks into completions of unrelated random prefills.

record.problems: For the broad-misalignment results, the study does not report matched benign fine-tune or base-model misalignment rates. Counts are mainly for the top-ranked completions, not a general neutral-question response rate. The authors dropped the coherency judge for these short random-prefill continuations; human validation of the adapted judge is reported, but no uncertainty estimates accompany the per-model emergent-misalignment counts.
record.rows_left_out: Other model-organism leakage results, including false facts and planted AuditBench behaviors, were left out because they measure their trained quirks rather than broad misalignment on unrelated prompts. The code-vulnerability result is included as a finding outside the listed versions.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune; no secure or educational controls.
Uses existing financial/medical/sports EM models but reports no misalignment rate against a base model or benign fine-tune; only detector-ranked counts.
No seeds, no coherence filter (dropped), no training-time tracking, and no effect size against a base model.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The EM models are known organisms used to validate a detector, and all EM numbers are counts among the method's own top-ranked completions. Figure 6 includes base models only for keyword matching, not the EM judge, so there is no base rate for misalignment. The coherency judge was dropped. Human validation of the adapted judge gave κ=0.758, with most disagreements between aligned and emergent misaligned. Table 3 gives per-configuration combined narrow+emergent counts, e.g. Qwen financial C4/Chat top-100 = 43, but these are also method performance.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test broad misalignment after insecure-code fine-tuning against the base model and matched secure-code or class-framed controls.

Tests bad financial, medical, and extreme-sports advice fine-tunes, but not harmless reward hacks or number sequences; does not compare the misalignment rate with matched benign fine-tunes or base-model rates.
Does not test misalignment arising from RL; KTO-trained AuditBench organisms are not evaluated for this claim’s broad misalignment outcome.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating broad misalignment.
Does not test inoculation framing or brief benign retraining as mitigations for broad misalignment.

Reports outcomes for two open-model sizes/families, but does not test training seeds, does not retain a coherence filter (the coherency judge was dropped), and does not track when during training the effect appears. Its main counts are among perplexity-ranked completions, not a general neutral-question response rate.
